title: The teams in the product: the walk on Home, the solution team on a project, every walk on Admin
request: Phase 6 (the owner): Home and the product: the board, the pauses answered on the page, the API for testers.
plan: A service the routes call: start or resume a walk once, read a walk without running it, list the walks.
Routes for drafts, projects and Admin.
A Team panel on Home and a Teams tab on Admin.
The critic's model only after the sealed gate.

decisions.decision: A step only when the person asks: the page reads the walk, and POST runs it to its next pause.
decisions.why: A walk waits on the person; nothing should run behind their back or twice.

decisions.decision: The pause shown is read from the pauses the walk writes, not from the checkpoint's internals.
decisions.why: The walk already writes each pause open and closes it: one source the page and the dataset both read.

decisions.decision: The critic's model serves only once the team passed its sealed gate.
decisions.why: The measurement decides what serves; until then the rules ask.

change: dclab_rnd/orchestra/service.py; GET/POST /api/drafts/{id}/team (draft/api.py), GET/POST /api/projects/{id}/team and GET /api/teams (agentic/pages/team.py, the owner's); Home's Team panel and Admin's Teams tab; the API client and the app rebuilt.

findings.defect: The Team panel showed nothing when the walk paused before its first hand-off.
findings.scenario: In the browser: the walk paused on the first question; the page said it had not walked yet.
findings.cause: The panel drew only when a board existed.
findings.fix: The panel shows the waiting pause whether or not a board was written.
findings.test: manual check in the app's browser (screenshots), tests/test_team_api.py

findings.defect: An ML engineer could open the holdout through the new project route.
findings.scenario: A data_scientist posted approve=true while the solution team waited on the holdout gate: the gate was approved and the programme read the holdout.
findings.cause: The route needed only write; the walk approved the gate as the person.
findings.fix: A resume of a holdout approval demands approve_gate (an owner or a reviewer).

findings.defect: The page showed a pause the walk no longer waited on.
findings.scenario: An empty answer ended the walk; the page still showed the question; answering it gave 409.
findings.cause: The pause was read from the last line of the pauses file, which a skipped question never closes.
findings.fix: The pause is read from the walk's checkpoint.

findings.defect: Starting again while a draft's walk waited threw the walk away.
findings.scenario: After two answers, POST {} restarted the walk from nothing; the first left orphaned boards and no record.
findings.cause: The walk did not guard a start against an open pause, as the solution team did.
findings.fix: A start while a pause waits returns that pause; a new walk starts on a fresh thread.

findings.defect: An answer was not checked against its pause.
findings.scenario: approve=false sent to the prediction moment's question recorded the moment as 'False'.
findings.fix: A question takes words, a confirmation or an approval a yes or no; anything else 422.

findings.defect: Two runs of a project's team could overlap.
findings.scenario: Two POSTs at the holdout approval both approved the gate; one approval stayed unused for a later read.
findings.cause: The project's running flag is set only inside the programme's run.
findings.fix: One walk of a project at a time (409 otherwise).

findings.defect: Items carried over from 28.3 were dropped silently.
findings.scenario: 28.3's Left moved the team switch and the per-run budget to 28.8; neither was built or listed.
findings.cause: The status was written from what was built.

findings.defect: An approval was asked without showing what it approves.
findings.scenario: Approve: understanding with Yes and No, the critic's concerns unseen, recorded as overridden.
findings.cause: The view dropped the pause's summary.
findings.fix: The pause's summary (the concerns, the parts, the build's state) shown, escaped.

findings.defect: Two quick resumes could lose a session from the walk's record.
findings.scenario: The state was read before the turn lock; the second request rewrote runs from a stale read; the spend and models under-counted.
findings.cause: The read and the walk were not under one lock; runs was overwritten.
findings.fix: The read is inside the turn; runs is appended by a reducer.

findings.defect: The busy check blocked the event loop on PostgreSQL.
findings.scenario: answering() opened a connection on the loop.
findings.cause: Called directly in the async route.
findings.fix: Run in a thread, as the message route does.

findings.defect: A test would fail the day the sealed team run passes.
findings.scenario: It asserted the critic's model never serves, from the repository's evidence.
findings.cause: A fact of the evidence asserted as a constant.

findings.defect: The dev corpus was not rebuilt.
findings.cause: make sft-dev not run after the record.
findings.fix: The dev corpus rebuilt with make sft-dev after the record.

findings.scenario: No test for the project route, a wrong answer, a restart, the holdout permission.
findings.cause: Only the happy path was tested.

outcome: A person can walk a draft with the team on Home, answer its pauses there, and the owner sees every walk on Admin.
lessons: A view of a paused process must show the pause even before the process has produced anything else.
A route that resumes a gate must demand the gate's own permission: the permission of the route is not the permission of the decision it carries.
Read a paused process's state from the process, never from a log that a skipped step does not close.
risks: The product's Build button still builds directly; the walk's approval is the team's own path until Home moves to the graph.
